Koi · car-cost ledger · design batch 2 · sheet 13 — last of the surface

Onboarding

Three beats, all skippable — and no account, ever, before the first fill
DRAWS    wireframes §11 · §1.4
READS    spec §C8 · D-006 · §I1
FIXTURE  the Golf, before it existed
DATE     2026-08-04
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT

No sync, no account, no passkey

Sync is opt-in from Settings only. Putting an account concept in beat one would contradict the product's own floor — fully functional local-only with no account — and would be a bigger, earlier commitment than anything here asks for.

Also absent: a tour, a permission prompt, a paywall, a "welcome back". The app opens onto a ledger you can use before it knows your name.

THE THREE FIELDS, NAMED

Make · model · fuel type

§C8 promises "three fields" without naming them. These three, because fuel type is load-bearing — it decides how economy is computed and which reminders even make sense — while the odometer arrives free with the first fill.

Asking for an odometer here would be asking someone to walk to their car during setup. It is the one number that captures itself.

THE HOLE IN "ONCE, NEVER AGAIN"

Beat 3 is anchored to the first car, not to onboarding

A reminder needs a carID. If the suggestion were tied to "onboarding ran", anyone who skipped beat 2 would burn it unshown — spending a once-ever offer on a screen that could not accept it.

So it fires after beat 2, after an import, or after a later Garage add — whichever comes first, exactly once.

01 · The three beats

No tab bar and no FAB — onboarding owns the whole screen until it hands over. Every beat has a visible way out.
BEAT 1 · THE VALUE LINE · §C8 VERBATIM
9:41
▮▮▮ ⌾ ▊
魚
Koi keeps your car's story.
Fills, services and reminders.
Computed honestly, kept on your phone.
Start Skip

"Computed honestly, kept on your phone" is the entire product promise in six words, and it is the only marketing sentence in the app. It earns its place by being true: article 4's derivations and the local-first default are both literal readings of it.

Skip is a real control, not a grey afterthought — accent-tinted type at full 44 pt. A skip that is hard to find is a dark pattern, and this screen has nothing to defend.

BEAT 2 · ADD A CAR · THREE FIELDS
9:41
▮▮▮ ⌾ ▊
Add your car
Three fields. Everything else can wait.
MAKE
VW
MODEL
Golf GTI
FUEL
Petrol Diesel Electric Hybrid
The odometer comes with your first fill. Nothing to look up now.
Save Import from MyCar Skip

The same form as Garage's add-car, minus everything below the rule — and minus the photo, which is a detour during setup. Not a parallel implementation — the "everything else" section is simply collapsed, so a field can never exist here and be missing there.

Fuel is a chip row, not free text — an enum entered by tapping, which is also the fix for the build writing fuel type as an unvalidated string. Import sits below Save: it is the rarer path, and offering it first would imply Koi expects you to arrive with data.

BEAT 3 · ONE SUGGESTION · ONCE, EVER · DARK
9:41
▮▮▮ ⌾ ▊
One reminder to start?
Spain's ITV inspection is due every year for cars over four years old.
You can change the date, or add your own later from any car.
Add it No thanks

One suggestion, and it explains itself. The ITV sentence is there because a driver new to Spain genuinely may not know the rule — the offer teaches rather than assuming. No thanks is persisted and respected: it never returns, on any car.

Refused: suggesting a second reminder, pre-ticking it, or showing it as a list of five with checkboxes. One offer is a courtesy; five is a setup wizard, and the product does not have those.

Skipping everything is a supported path

Skip on beat 1 and beat 2 lands on Home's zero-car state — "Add your car to begin." — which is a complete, usable screen, not a punishment. Beat 3 has not been spent, because no car exists yet to attach a reminder to.

It fires later, on the first car added from Garage. That is the whole reason the anchor is "a car exists" and not "onboarding ran".

The second device must not be told to add a car

Waiting for your records to arrive.
Sync is on. This usually takes a moment.

When syncEnabled && !hasSynced, the zero-car copy changes. "Add your car to begin" on a phone that is about to receive a car produces a duplicate the architecture deliberately will not auto-merge — one sentence prevents it.

Where the first fill happens

Not in onboarding. Beat 3 hands over to Home, and the fill is captured through the ordinary + — the same keypad it will be for the next thousand fills. It gets the app’s one spring — the saved moment — the same on the first fill as on the thousandth. The spring is for the record landing, not for the user’s behaviour, so it belongs in the real surface rather than in a tutorial.

What the first fill cannot yet say

Its record page reads "Not measured yet — two full tanks with odometers measure your first number." with two progress dots, one filled. Koi's first honest act is to admit it does not know your economy yet, on the very screen a lesser app would put a fabricated figure.

02 · Batch 2 complete — what the thirteen sheets now cover

Every surface in wireframes.md §1 – §11 is drawn on one reconciled fixture, with both themes shown wherever the palette is load-bearing.
Foundations · 01–03, 08
The authored dark palette with every pair AA-validated. The control language — rows, wells, chips, buttons, toasts, layers, the chart grammar and its table-first form. The four-tab shell and its depth ladder. And the accent sheet, which moved emphasis to ink so the one green means fuel and nothing else.
The tabs · 04–05, 09–10
Garage and the car page in both ownership shapes. Home's four states. History's ledger with the plan row that makes July reconcile. Insights' four lenses, drawn as stat tables first.
The tasks · 06–07, 11–13
Settings and Sync. Capture and the odometer sheet. The record pages and their computed panels. Reminders and Insurance & papers. This sheet.
Two annexes · A and B
A · the degraded states, every enumerated one, none of them styled as an error. B · the icon-well exploration that replaced emoji with a tinted well and a thin-stroke set. decisions.md logs every open question taken and every arithmetic correction made.
Sheet 13 of 13 — the surface is complete. What is not designed here, named so it is not mistaken for an omission: the MyCar import mapping screens, the paper viewer, and the export writers. All three sit behind features the build has not installed, and each needs its own pass with real data in front of it.
